rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm checked: an unresolved referent leaves a projected slide unfollowable; not present. Sequential read of all 7 chunks. Chunk 0 L3 'the system that built the workbook you're sitting in' names its own referent in the same clause -- not a forward-pointing tease. Chunk 1 L7 'Agentic systems become visible...' is self-contained. Chunk 2's four LO bullets (L13-16) are each self-contained; L16's 'the loop that makes the system improve' is unpacked in the same bullet by the colon-list that follows it. Chunk 3 L22 'The actual system behind this workbook' reuses 'system' from chunks 0/1 (same-file reuse, explicitly not a violation) and 'this workbook' is a plain deictic to the document itself. Chunk 4 is a bare structural include link, no prose referent to resolve. Chunk 5's five bullets (L30-34) are each self-contained factual claims; L34's 'The customer workbook' reuses the workbook/system frame from chunks 0-3 and matches the maintainer block's own 'client output' gloss on the demo spine. Chunk 6 L38 'run one together' -- checked as a candidate vague-pronoun case: 'one' takes its antecedent from 'the shape of a system' three words earlier in the SAME sentence (ordinary English anaphoric 'one' substitution, e.g. 'you've seen a car, now drive one'), not a stranded or never-named referent. No never-named or vague-with-full-history referent found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm checked: repo/maintainer vocabulary a room can't parse. `grep -inE '\bcompendium\b|\bforcing function\b|\bsurface\b|\bbeat[s]?\b|\bmood\b|Connections|\bfiring\b' curriculum/evals/body-views/claude-basics--module--agentic-systems-repo-demo.body.txt` run this session -> 0 hits. Closest call: chunk 2 L16 'compound' as the seventh verb in 'the loop that makes the system improve: rules, inspect, plan, edit, check, build, compound.' Scored PASS under the §8 display-vs-communicate test: this module's entire premise is showing the student the actual repo/system that produced the workbook (maintainer 'Demo spine' ends on 'checks -> compounding'), so the loop is exhibited as an observed fact of the real system the live demo shows, not planted as vocabulary the student is expected to adopt; the word itself ('build on itself over time') is also plain enough English for the rollout-custodian audience, unlike compendium/forcing-function-class shorthand. 'customer versions' (L7), 'customer workbook' (L34), and 'build scripts' (L7) are ordinary IT-audience vocabulary, not repo-internal terms.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.

Scored under the §9 'What You'll Learn bullets' carve-out even though this training's heading reads 'What This Workshop Builds' rather than the generic template name: `curriculum/trainings/claude-basics/where-is-this-all-going.md` L7-14 uses the identical heading with the identical `- **[verb]** [thing]` shape (module-shape.md's LO template), confirming this is claude-basics's own name for the canonical LO section, not a different kind of list. The bolded verb IS the template; the per-slide count is the template's doing, not an authored emphasis choice. Zero bold anywhere in chunks 0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm checked: a bullet that reads as rigour but adds nothing the slide does not already hold. A system is...' was the closest candidate -- it draws a chat-vs-system contrast that is NOT stated in the Big Idea (chunk 1 lists artifacts, never names 'chat' as the contrast term), so it introduces the frame the remaining four What-to-Notice bullets exemplify, rather than re-announcing something that already did its work. (b) self-referential design commentary: none of the 9 bullets describe the training's own pedagogy to the student (grep -niE 'by design|before the training names|encounter the problem' -> 0 hits). (c) aphorism kicker: L34 (the section's last bullet) states a new build/deploy fact, not a koan restating the 'What to Notice' header or a **The point:** line -- no such line exists in this file.
